$BTC

The second 10-week signal - an update

Alright, it's weekend, the range continues further and we managed our way into four trades so far, of which 3 wins, 1 pending (2 TP's in so far), ever since giving the second 10 week signal at 109k.

That signal, I mentioned, is a clear call that we will see across-the-board higher prices after it lapses (which you will feel), and in theory, it ends begin November.

Unfortunately though, in the process, the market looked really euphoric at 125k with all the ATH celebrations, bulk longs and relentless buying happening without price moving, I am sure you remember it as if it was Yesterday.

As you know, we adjusted course slightly and closed our longs with a loud and proud announcement at the time, soon enough, the market dropped hard.

Personally, I did not see it make new lows after closing those longs, and expected just a standard-aggressive drop where the 10 week signal holds. And although I'm not complaining for getting cheaper prices again, it does mean we will have to wait longer for the 10 week signal to complete.

That is because the 10 week signal is cyclically based, part of the final weekly cycles in the framework of the bigger bull-cycle (which we are still in), and is, just like any cycle, reset each time new lows are made.

And so because we have made a new low at the start of October, that means the cyclical count is indeed reset, and alongside, the reset of the 10-week count, starting the 10th of October. That also means it is expected to end around the 19th of December now.

Could my estimate be wrong again on this? Yes. If we make new lows again, then the count has to be reset again, as the drop after the first 10 week signal was given, is still in progress in that case and will continue to until no new lows are made.

So the question remains: do I think new lows are coming on $BTC?

You already know my thoughts on that and I repeat that the answer most likely IMO is still no.

That's why we closed shorts at 106k and went long simultaneously, with the backbone and analysis given at the time.

I also give the final disclaimer that December 19th is just an estimate. It's by no means an exact time of expecting the exact top to happen or anything like that.

But it does mean a kind wink to all the cyclical top callers out there, alongside the callers who say alts won't do well near the end of the cycle, who are more occupied with disqualifying the bull-cycle instead of qualifying it, IMO, too early at the exact wrong times. And it does disqualify all the traders showing their charts again of "planning to enter when price hits sub 100k, sub 90k, even sub 80k", as if we have all the time in the world to wait for that.

We will have to see who is "right". But regardless, here is another piece of my thoughts on the mid-high timeframe projection of the weeks ahead.

Enjoy.

Some alts do worse than what the $BTC.D movement reflects, some do better. On average, $BTC.D mirrors the opposite of the alt movement accurately.

Alright, so we had a big and fast spike in $BTC.D, which IMO completes the general framework of the bearish retest of our general plan that $BTC.D has already topped at 65%, which means the best entries on the average healthy alt bag (not cherry picked, keyword, average) are already gone, and although recently they have gone close to those better entries, they still didn't reach them.

To give some more context, we called the top at 64% to be around this area of 64% (we did this in May 2025, scroll on my timeline for transparency and in name of the principle to always fact check everything even if it's from me).

So far so good, and with the recent spike, no reaching above 65% and the spike quickly retraced, nothing has changed on that front.

But at the time of it happening, things looked scary so my last post was focused on easing your mind in the midst of the carnage, that $BTC.D would quickly retrace to 60% and show some weakness very soon (while it was at 62%, see quoted tweet), and we have seen that weakness so far which was important to me, because it confirms this was indeed a bearish retest.

The string of quoted tweets documents my high timeframe thoughts carefully step by step within the framework of our high timeframe plan of the $BTC.D top at 65%, and once the top formation is completed, the alt strength we have been waiting for would come.

But with the large influx recently of people telling me there will be no alt season this cycle, and with many large influencers who keep on repeating and repeating that alts are not ideal to hold, I like to share my low timeframe view to ease you through the immediate uncertainty (I know how much posts of anyone are easy to frame change your mind around even if their charts are hand wavy or backed by little data).

Low timeframe view

The good news is, the spike up is fast which is in perfect alignment with a classic bear market retest (see my last post before this post).

The other good news is, if you are still holding the majority of your altcoin position value now like myself, or are planning to reposition what you have released, you have survived most of the pain and shown resilience.

This pain was indeed the spike/the fast pain.

The bad news is, in markets, fast pain is on the occasion followed by slow pain. This pain is no worse than the fast pain financially speaking, but emotionally speaking a second test to your conviction.

So in the same way begin Feb '25 had a fast spike, and from begin May, the slower pain followed to form the general top (still the top and will remain the top imo), now, we may see the same on the retest.

No guarantees, and I'd rather not see it, this is just a worst case scenario.

In any case, that is good news because it implies we overall move within the range I have drawn out, before breaking down further, whilst $BTC moves in its range we have planned before, before breaking up further.

So if you survived the fast pain, you will be able to survive the slow pain (if it comes), until ultimately, $BTC.D breaking down and reaching our second target of 55%.

Take-aways

And as final words, I am highly convinced we will break down. Our first target of 60% is already reached, confirming local weakness that this in fact is a bearish retest (which also confirms the top).

And that we will have "an alt season", in my humble view.

To get there, in the immediate future, I have drawn out what the worst is that could happen, anything else, is a lot better.

But calling off alt season is not appropriate IMO, I personally picked up some more heavy spot bags, and likely will pick up some altcoin challenge positions too in the near future.

Enjoy, these are my thoughts. IMO it continues to make sense to stay healthily bullish (in modest leverage terms).

tweets.text:
"So Astro, does that mean the top is close, should we start selling already?"

Although I do think time-wise, the top is fairly close, I don't think it's worth selling $ETH and especially alts yet. (In terms of $BTC spot, sure, taking some profits makes sense, I have sold about 10% of my cyclical bag)

But alts usually go sideways for years before in the final months, putting in the majority of the gains.

Not the rule and more the guideline, but all alt charts on non-log scale look that way.

And the reason this happens is simply because of their thin liquidity. Accumulation takes time, and keeping the price quiet before the big moves creates complacency (i.e. awareness without taking action).

"Ah, not going to buy yet, going to wait for one more crash"

That complacency is what later fuels into fomo later, especially if it takes so long. And that fomo is the opposite end liquidity when it's time to sell (not during the pump itself for the majority).

That's how I still see this cycle continue. Where the alts rise in a short period of time, making the months we have been holding, where so far only sublte gains against usd and btc have been made, suddenly very obviously worthwhile.

And it's why I have put so much stress since the 65% $BTC.D top call we made during the very 30 day period of the $BTC.D top itself, to not enter this stage empty handed.

$BTC macro update

Push up completed ✅, on to the final stages

It has been a while since I updated my macro perspective.

Primarily because not much has changed, secondarily because the 10 week signal posts took over for a while.

But here is a deep rehash, no pun intended.

Because the hash ribbons, amongst other indications (not "indicators") were indeed a big part of this most recent bottom, as well as the parabolic 2017-model bull market arc (looking like a straight line on the parabolic chart), as well as the 1-2 macro gap model (not drawn here, see older posts), as well as the cyclical timing, and the dynamics between altcoins, $ETH and $BTC, and finally, the sentiment.

They all combined into our analysis, being able to confidently tell you where the market will go next on the high timeframes each and every market update for a few years now, on $BTC, $ETH and alts.

This in essence, is the summary of our bull market masterplan, used to make every important move we make count.

Further analysis

Most importantly, a recent weekly low is planted at the time we called the bottom. Since we're at the end of the bull run, it triggered a new 10 week signal.

We are also getting very close into the topping zone we planned out in 2023, lower boundary being 140k as an absolute minimal target.

Will I adjust this zone? Time is more important than price, so if price moves higher, earlier, that's okay and I will adapt. But I certainly will start selling those ancient cyclical spot bags as we reach the higher end of it, with $BTC and $ETH earlier, and alts as late as possible.

The recent bottom also held the parabolic arc (straight line on this logarithmic chart), and the plan rolled out of the $BTC dominance for the majority of the first cycle, transitioning to $ETH dominance and strength, now slowly turning into alt dominance (as you will see), is nearly completely fulfilled.

Indeed, #alt dominance is getting close and although you can't "feel" it yet emotionally, you can feel it numerically (see my previous post on it), alts have already taken over and the altcoin waiters are already losing out since $BTC.D has topped at 65%. A top that will not be threatened in any way IMO. The 70% callers will soon convert to 65% callers, maybe even 60%+ callers, signs they are capitulating.

My positions (the action)

This masterplan is why I continue to stay bullish on $BTC, $ETH and alts on the high timeframes, and continue to frame trade ideas upon that.

It's why I continue to hold the final bits of the current second $BTC long, the $ETH long from 1.8k, the $ETH long from the 4k's and all altcoin positional longs and altcoin challenge longs.

That is the bread and butter gain I aim to carry further. No major short positions yet. The last major short we took was in Feb 2025 and the plenty of shorts in March - Aug 2024. I'm more focused on taking profit at the right times as a way to ride the market optimally.

Final words

Use this macro plan as a guideline to base your investments and lower timeframe positions upon. Not an exact prediction, do not take the line I draw out in a literal sense. It's drawn to stay in line with where the market is headed, the nature of the pullbacks (how deep, shallow, short, long), and moves up (how high, and how long they last). )Literal fractals do not work).

That way, you'll never be surprised to what happens, and you have a detailed plan to assess clearly when it's wrong.

Exactly the way I operate. With the honors of being on track for years now.

tweets.text:
Detaching ego from trading is hard in many ways.

It's what hinders you from taking the right trade rather than just being "right".

From personal experience, the most effective remedy is a bit tricky and I'll try to explain. But for starters, it's not what you mostly hear. It's not: 

By avoiding looking at your pnl (how are you going to monitor trades then)
By avoiding the charts (how are you going to monitor trades then)
Or avoiding X, the opinions of others (others are everywhere, we are social creatures, and X is one of your sources of learning probably)

Instead, it's good to recognise that:

When price goes one way, it always feels as it it's the biggest deal.

The spectacle and anticipation is always very high on every move. A lot of people on this platform are very rich and/or go very high risk and so it's a big deal for them if they are right or wrong.

Reflects in the emotion running high.

Sounds cliché, but if you look at your own pnl, as long as you risk what is fine for you and accept where you are at, it allows you to eliminate the anticipation and eliminate the feeling of every move being such a big deal. 

Because it's not.

It's just an illusion as if you missed out forever on something. But you didn't.

Real results, come from consistently and neutrally observing and taking action, observing and taking action, observing again and taking action. Avoiding as many mistakes as possible (a few are tolerable).

That shift in thinking turns your sleepless nights into just a little bit of healthy thrill or sadness every move.

Yes trading is hard. But the difficulty is not in getting every trade right. It's in getting most right and making money consistently.

One move, is no big deal. Your attitude inside of each one, is a big deal.

Nice move up so far, the slow reversal continuing, and the double-range setup in play. A few reminders.

Quick update on $BTC.

Because I see what you’re saying. “This looks like a bearish retest.” “A bear flag.” “A corrective move up.” Certainly on the local view. So I’m simply going to expand on the slow-reversal idea we’ve been sticking with.

This will be a summary of the key elements I mentioned over the last few days, both in setting that important low and in the recent trade we’re in, along with some clarification to help you through this stage of the move.

I also had some questions about the “slow reversal,” why it’s taking so long, and how to actually play it. And some questions about how I derive my zones. I’ll address all of that with a short, clearer version here.

Large POI – Slow reversals – Double ranges

When price hits a large POI, it takes time to react. It has to, simply because larger players need time to accumulate while simultaneously keeping everyone hesitant. These are naturally slow reversals, and with them comes the use of the double-range setup.

I don’t often share this openly, but long-term followers know what a double range is. The construct is always tied to slow reversals. We also used it on the higher timeframe to call the intermediate Solana top in March 2024, as well as the breakout out of it. That too was a slow process, re-accumulation rather than accumulation.

On that note, special thanks to TradingView for finally implementing the 0.25 and 0.75 on their parallel-channel tool within my most beloved concept, ranges. You know how much I value ranges, both as a tool and as a point of reference for breakouts. Only real ranges give real breakouts.

The 0.25 and 0.75 are important because that’s precisely what the double-range construct is. It’s nothing more than a range above another range, right next to each other. Or, viewed differently, a larger range with more granularity. So not just a range low (0%), a range high (100%), and a mid (50%), but also the 0.25 and 0.75. They are Gann levels fused with my range theorem, and I simply consider them a double range because it blends perfectly with modern price concepts like deviations (a deviation from the lower range is an entry into the upper one) along with other benefits I’ll expand on later.

This explains why I placed our grey box where it is, at the 0.5. I hoped that level would form a significant bottom to at least range-high 97k (the 0), but price tapped the 0.75 (93k) first before going deeper.

Knowing exactly how price moves within a slow reversal using this range is difficult and requires close monitoring of the intraday structure and sessions. Always use confluence.

Using this range to determine what comes next is the key to the entire outlook. A breakdown is bad; a break to the upside is good, especially if we get a pre-breakout consolidation at midrange. I still think we break to the upside, regardless of the last trade’s result, but of course I’ll humbly accept a break to the downside. My money remains on a break up, and this range will help us decide early which way it goes. But again, I think it’s up.

Never let past trades affect future analysis. Use analysis to project future positioning. Losing a trade doesn’t mean flipping a bias, that’s letting ego get involved. Best to continue observing what the chart tells you, then conclude and execute accordingly. That’s exactly why I took a new trade at the 0.25 a few posts ago.

The answer still leads higher, working through this range first.

Eyes also on the FOMC date coming up, as you know, by the time FOMC comes, the low is already in.

And still keeping in mind the 91% chance of no new weekly closes below the low.

To recap; TLDR

Further clarification of this purple POI through the double-range construct, why it’s tied to slow reversals, and how to play it. It also frames why I remain bullish, why this purple POI likely holds, and how I see the slow reversal continuing.

Slow, but still a reversal. Both upper targets of 112k and ATH remain in play, and $BTC bears and flip-floppers will keep calling for 70k or lower at the worst possible time. (Same with alt bears on BTC.D calling for a cyclical high.)

I’ve seen none of that yet, and I’m not seeing signs of it now, at least not for the next high-timeframe move.

Regardless, there’s no point in calling for a bearish retest right here anyways. You have to ask: is shorting smart even if you expect a retest? Or am I simply playing into sentiment? Shouldn’t I be long or bullish here instead? That “retest” may lead straight into a new ATH. Because time and price now are right to buy. And money is only made by predicting the next move. Waiting for a retest doesn’t make money. And that is exactly why this projected “retest” happens in the first place (though I don’t think we get it).

I could always be wrong, and I’ll adjust if needed. All of this is NFA. But for now, the slow-reversal idea has been the idea for a while, and I expect it to remain the idea for a while.

Has some flaws executing on this idea recently in getting into this trade, but the analysis remains intact.

And we will bring it home in the name of my core analysis components.

$BTC - There is a 91% chance the weekly bottom is in (plus or minus a sweep).

In other words, 91% chance there will be no weekly closes below the current low.

Fear is everywhere. People talking about waiting out the price action, telling you the bull run is over, telling you to be on the sidelines.

This post is not saying new ATH's are guaranteed to come. For that, I will provide other analysis.

We first need to call the bottom before even thinking about new ATH's. Yes, I do promise new ATH's. But this post is not about that. This post is about not selling, about not falling for the sentiment that the "bull run is over" and about instead getting excited about these prices. Because, the fear is all just a narrative.

One that didn't arise at 125k, one that didn't even arise when we were at 110k and kept dropping.

None of that was called for, and here it is, the sentiment in full swing, suddenly, and at the worst time.

So this post isn't only to silence the "it's over" or "be careful" or "wait for the trend" posts (whether subtly or loudly), but also to, if the bear market indeed started, to prevent you from selling now (nfa) at the worst time. Because once we do get the move I keep on calling and calling and calling, the narrative will change again. "The bull run is back", "The trend has shifted", and all other quotes that promote you to buy high, sell higher, or more frequently : panic sell lower.

Indeed, this post is telling you to NOT wait for the trend change. Because that will just sucker you in on the next local high.

Selling now, is going with the sentiment, and waiting for the trend to change is also going with the sentiment.

So no matter where you entered or are yet to enter, I have good news, because one of my core chart elements tells me there will be no weekly closes anymore below the current low, before seeing 112k and + (118k) with a 91% chance.

So forget about waiting for the "trend", or being careful, or fearing your hold in essence from reading the in-between-the-lines of almost every post out there. I have an analysis telling you the exact opposite, to help you get in before the trend. (Buy before the trend, sell into the trend).

The analysis

It's one of my favorite types of analyses, the one of capitulation volume. "True capitulation" is where high volume sells, and gets absorbed by even higher volume. The extraction of large funds and companies (the whale degens i.e. the victims) by liquidity generating whales (the winners)

So how do we find capitulation volume? It's again the rule of three, which is everywhere in trading markets.

For those reasons, this rule is also often abused and overused. Trading isn't as simple as "just use the rule of three". So I like to do my own approach called "the layered rule of three", layered underneath an effective trait of markets.

Here, the layer is the volume of weekly (=bull-bear cycle core timeframe) candles. 

So the essence here of the layered rule of three is simple: if three candles in a row go red with respectable volume peaking above all else, that's capitulation and a bottom.

The complexity of this analysis goes beyond it, and it's a bit more nuanced (two small candles could add to large ones, and small green volume candles or retests do not reset the three-in-a-row red streak)

But other than that, in simple terms: that's it.

I always encourage you to back test and crosscheck for yourself what the action looked like in history. Never believe anything randomly without getting the feel and nature of it yourself first. So for your own reference, I'm giving you the weekly candles where it happened before according to my calibration (with local order flow verification, just as confirmation, not relevant here):

31 March 2025
2 Sep 2024
17 Jan 2022
21 Jun 2021
9 March 2020
18 Nov 2019
26 March 2018
17 Aug 2015
11 Aug 2014
2 more dates prior, not given

They all give the pre-historic capitulation volume (on aggregated spot volume BTC:INDEX charts). And from the closes of these candles, price moved either

➡️At least 35% before continuing the bear market (would lead us to 118k) (2 out of 11 times) when ignoring the covid crash which was just a short term shakeout)
➡️Or new ATH's, continuing the bull run (8 out of 11 times)
➡️Or kept going down (1 out of 11 times)

So that also answers from one statistical angle that the bull run is not over with a probability of 75%.
Add that on top of the 112k is 99% certainly coming, as you know I am very confident in that level.
And 118k (the 35% move), has a 91% chance of coming, as per analysis here (10/11 = 91%).

Summary

So that's it. A very strong and daring call to tell you the bottom is close, no new weekly closes below the current weekly low (a small wick below is possible, who cares), before 112k with a 99% chance, 118k with a 91% chance (this analysis), and the bull run continuing with a chance of 75% chance (new ath's).

That is just 1 statistic. There is way, way more to it.

I spend 12 hours a day (re)fin(d)ing these. Here is just another big one to give you a strong idea, continuing the theses, despite my mistake of closing the last long.

Analysis still holds, execution mistakes are always possible, the sized and fresh large capital from selling other type of assets is reopened on spot instead and is the current one being run in the journey of trades.

Hope this clears up the timeline of all the "trend shift waiters" or bear market believers.

Enjoy.

My $BTC trades - a transparent review + quick reminder where to next

4 wins, 2 losses

Context

Alright, we had an interesting time trading the last two months. With standard losses, a bigger loss, smaller victories and bigger victories.

It started off with wins, 4 times in a row, then two losses. We had an intense time experiencing a wide array of emotions this entire process.

Every trade you see on the chart, is both matched in time (the time where the trade starts is where I started) and price (or average entry price if multiple entries are taken), each time where I projected invalidation, target or projected target (if it was a loss)

Everything is documented by the way on my timeline. Fully transparent and always in live time. There is no arguing about these calls, and as you know, I think that's key.

Posting any trade that "I took alone", has 0 value because it can be completely fake. PnL screenshots are often photoshopped and with AI these days, it's easier than ever to do so.

Nothing beats in-live-time timestamps and clarity of calls (one-directional-consistency, minimal hedging) on a consistent basis, both to believe posts, and to identify consistent traders.

Review

The first trade was well identified, our "final reversal zone" identified both the final bottom as well as the move to 125k where we loudly fully closed longs in anticipation for a longer lasting top.

After the drop happened, and where I initially believed the low would be plus or minus a sweep, close to it into a key POI, a new long made sense, just playing for the bounce into the 50% retrace along with very frothy "I missed the bottom" longs at the top of 115k. Sentiment also aligning (you should have seen the timeline by then). And so along with all other reasons already mentioned into that post, it made sense at that exact time and price to trade it back down to range low as part of our range idea.

Executed, then once wick low reached, a sweep back up made sense due to local order flow, range low being present, trade it back to at least midrange.

At least midrange happened again, but no higher. Sadly. I certainly expected higher but that was our exact FOMC reversal time where price very likely were to trade back down. Froth also very high (you should have seen the timeline again then), same POI showing the same signatures again, seeing SFP's again, late in the month, so had to close longs again and wait for a better entry and let price drop.

Then came the losses. FOMC reversals are strong, this is our own edge we created. And this also answered the question further with what I meant with "this long may take time, this is going to be a tough long, we need a slow and passive trade management along with it".

It sadly took quite a bit longer than I initially projected for all those reasons.

Didn't expect price to hit our purple POI just like that, but here we are. Every single low timeframe low we called, ended up being just that - a low timeframe POI. And where the standard trader on here on X just posts "we will bounce here", he may end up being right, with sometimes faked PnL's after the fact, looks like a genius. But in reality, a call and a trade are two different things. I have shown that very clearly. Every low we called, was nothing but a low timeframe low before price headed lower, not good for the high timeframe long. So, I was "right" every time, but didn't make money - clearly two different things.

So had to take a first loss where we also doubled up, so that was a bigger loss (counting for two).

Then, I showed my conviction in one direction - back up. We are reached 112k, the old midrange, a very common move and I haven't fully explained why I want that level. One reason is old midranges get retraced very often after sharp down moves into pivotal news events. And there is more to it. But anyway...

We showed conviction, I don't change bias easily. We entered a second long, with the warning that this will be a very low-pace, multiple entries of very low size, building up to 1 full size long.

It all went well, we took entries step by step, convicted we will reverse back up (very slowly, we called it a slow reversal post after post). But then I misread the action at the very wick low, not seeing orders come in at the same time trading to the bottom end of our purple POI, so went ahead and closed out at pretty much the exact low, announcing it at the same time. Why did I do that? Because it was a mistake and nothing else.

Where to next?

Because right after the exit, just 1% higher, it quickly developed into the type demand I wanted to see into my purple POI so made the post that I am still very convinced in this being the low.

And my thesis of this very week being the last week of very strong downside, keeps holding our "112k is coming" thesis, strong.

It's still ways away form a full reversal (we are in a slow reversal). But "full reversals" only make sense after the fact. We always aim to call them before they happen, just like we have done with the last 4 trades, and tried to do with the last two trades.

So the story of those last two trades is unfinished. And that is why I took the same type of trade but with spot instead. Maybe I will strengthen that trade again with a long if a better entry comes along. But nothing recklessly.

But this spot trade is the next one in the series and we will see how it plays out.

My full review, it's been a journey. Good plays, some bad plays. Won about 10 RR, lost about 5 RR if accounting for price movement and double-up size on that 1 long, maybe a bit too much for two trades. Could have been up a massive amount of RR taken with size too, but ended up being a less than moderate few months of trading (5RR in two months). Ah well.

But like I said, the story of this last trade isn't finished yet. Aiming to bring it home strongly because and nothing in my system tells this isn't close to the bottom and nothing tells us the bear market is here.

tweets.text:
Success is adhering to the paradox of trading.

No matter how confident you are in your trade, never risk it all. Only up to medium risk is ok if done deliberately imo.

But then it's about building conviction through your analysis as high as you can by going broad into the right and not the wrong areas (secrets).

Then channel that conviction mostly into holding strongly, not into large size.

The larger the size, the harder to hold strongly, so both are additive towards the limited resource of conviction that you have built in your analysis.

Analyze, build conviction and become very confident. And then enter as if you're going to lose.

That is the paradox of trading.

$BTC

Trade frame and idea going forward: the bull market is not over

So, after the large down move and for a big part, being part of that, setting us back the streak gains we made in the last 4 trades before that, I made clear Yesterday that I am still bullish, still expect 112k and still believe the bull market isn't over.

Reasons

The reasons are that 112k is still a wide and open untouched magnet, we are in a higher low area, the top is not in according to any of my core system signals, so neither does this final drop start the bear market unlike what we are hearing everywhere now.

Finally and as mentioned last post, I repeat that the time and price pattern structure of this weekly candle strongly tells us that this is the last weekly downside candle, after which we range and go up again IMO. Sweeps of the current low could happen within that frame, but no breakdowns further like we had the past couple days/weeks, only fake moves that likely reclaim and form large opportunity.

I have more reasons why I believe price doesn't go much lower, but these are the core ones.

Sentiment

I also remind you that the sentiment again stays low. Popular accounts talking about bear markets, spot capitulation in a higher low area, and lots of "it's all over" from typical flip-flop accounts that don't really trade. Also having serious news headlines as if crypto is no longer a good investment on many NY large-fund bulletin boards.

In this slow reversal process, for sentiment to materialize against itself takes time. But time has already taken a while, and with my system aligning better now, it shouldn't be too much longer.

How I play it

You know my recent story. Had a fair few wins, but then two bigger losses. And so I'm not going to be in leverage for a while. 
Catching a large move is possible but not always easy with leverage, so just taking a step back to regain rhythm.

At the same time, you didn't like the idea of no clear invalidation. So here you go, a clear inval-entry-exit type of trade. Not saying the stop shown on this chart is exactly where I have put mine. But it serves as a clear and proper invalidation where I will exit close against, so here you go.

It still carries a risk if we were being hunted last trades, to also be hunted. But high timeframe moves like this are very hard to manipulate and target just one person + followers on this platform of although I am one of the few still sharing clear trades on this entire space by the looks of it, we'll see how it plays along the way and I'm currently looking for signs of possible hunts on last trades.

So this is just an entry taking by buying spot with funds I normally don't have in crypto but moved today. It's a wider stop, paired with a wider move aimed to be caught. The overall trade is still around 2 RR however. Nothing flashy, very boring indeed, just another type of trade I like going for, as you know by now, most my trades have been between 1RR-3RR. No 10R+ type of unrealistic models, largely offset by fees, funding and slippage anyway with tight stops.

On this trade, no partials will be taken, this is one and done.

Final words

Feel free to take this trade as you wish spot or lev (nfa). But this is just what I plan to do going forward. Step back from leverage, play spot and slowing it down. Whilst staying in the market and keeping the same frame and bias I have been keeping and still believe in firmly.

Also making a very clear statement that the bull run isn't over. Because if this move happens and we are back at 112k (first target), no one will talk about the bear market anymore. And my job to erase your belief in the future, already presented now in advance, will be done.

Enjoy.

86k so far, my proceeding thoughts on this reversal process back up...

...and the reality of catching a big move and playing a slow reversal trade and why I chose a slow entry strategy for it

The short answer to the question below: no, it's not a bottom call, it's a "the bottoming range is here" call. What this 86k level is though in my books is likely another low worth catching and tying the final entries for our trade upon. And so I entered final portions. Because this point is close to the time and price of the actual bottom.

It's been a while when I first started this trade as we are filling this trade very slowly and methodically. But a loose passive trading strategy is not about trying to nail the exact bottom. It's about aiming to catch every single low timeframe significant low coming in close to the bottom, before the reversal settles and offers a big move to have an as optimal entry as possible.

That not only keeps leverage low (90% of traders lever too high too soon), but also builds psychological edge, and forces you to stay in tune with the market and monitor the trade deliberately.

No, it doesn't look as great to showcase. It's not a flashy 1% SL gigantic million$ trade caught with 0 drawdown. Every single bottom, we do see those flashy "I nailed the bottom with a 1% SL" pop up after it already happened. Rarely showing the SL's eaten every single low timeframe POI before. That's not consistent trading in my book and doesn't actually make money - I just see as void entertainment.

So I aim with this trade to show the reality of trading, especially for long and drawn out reversals like this one.

We have so far have taken the following entries for this trade:

➡️The low at 93k on Nov the 16th NY time: half size
➡️The low at 89k Wednesday 18 November
➡️And now on Thursday 19 November, 86k

And the bottom may still end up lower, still inside our POI, but we are in the bottoming range.

So yes, it all looks rough when the action happens. But that's the fundamental reason of why many are scared to take action/ruin their "reputation" on this platform, or for their personal accounts.

Everyone wants an entry that is up immediately and never goes under, straight to profit, and fast too. I am aware I usually succeeded in this in most ways as well as with the last 4 wins.

But with this long and especially with slow reversal, that's not a smart way of approach, once again.

So I hope this graph makes sense. This is what this type of reversal feels like in real time, looks like and acts like every step along the way and how I act upon it every step along the way. It looks simple, and certainly does after it all happened. But in reality, the process isn't as simple as many make seem on here.

So yes, if it doesn't make sense yet, it will make a lot more sense once it all played out.

Sadly, because trades indeed always "make the most sense" after they happened. Yet it's all about positioning correctly before the actual move.

tweets.text:
Unpopular opinion, but RR is highly over rated, win rate is highly under rated.

High RR does look good on social media (where only selective winners are shown, with massive RR's scored).

But in the real world, higher win rate:

- gives you more confidence
- allows you to risk more
-allows for higher frequency of trading (get out sooner, get back in sooner)
- higher frequency and win rate gives you more instant feedback (if a high win rate edge fails, that's a bigger red flag than a low win rate high RR edge failing, ie., that is more valuable feedback), whether your edge works (or doesn't) - very key in trading, a lot of edge on this platform is faulty.

This is true in trading, investing, probably anything you do in life too. Going for smaller steps and building your life is probably better than trying to go for one gigantic beyond-the-moon step and failing years to do so in the process beforehand.

So despite how "fantastic" it sounds as a written story to hit home runs and perform long grinds with no reward until the home run gain, incremental gain is more stable, mentally and realistically especially in finance.

Those bigger steps, only come once strong foundations are in place.

Focus on win rate first, then RR second.

$BTC - sentiment

How it's highly bearish right now, and how I perform this read, part 2 - a more detailed post

You truly enjoyed the last post, so going to expand further on how I read and record sentiment. This is going to be a longer post. As you know, detail matters, and reading sentiment is a fine art. But it's not as hard as often portrayed, and a very good idea to learn it asap.

Not only because crypto/$BTC is one of the most straightforward asset classes to read sentiment and put to use, but commenting on sentiment is also very relevant right now into this (IMO) bottoming range, the low 80 k's, with one of the most clear sentiment reads out there we probably had this year.

You know my practice is to call out market situations in live time, perform deep analysis (both charts and sentiment), make a clear statement and provide you the pieces of the puzzles one by one, without changing stance once unless I have severe and drastic reasons to. We had the fortune to not have to have change stance before. And similarly, no reason has been given to change stance in the bottoming range once again, right here.

Recently for example, we have done the bearish version stance at 125k, loudly closing our longs, providing the silver pocket as final target for the leg, and highlighting the sentiment of loud ath celebrations.

And present time, we are doing the bullish version now, with our weekly bottom call in the low 80's, calling this weekly range a bottoming range. We will be highlighting the clear bearish sentiment n this range, and highlighting why being bearish is wrong, also explaining why people are bearish, and explaining how I get to a "clear" bearish read.

The answer is not "everyone is bearish so I am bullish", as we so ever so often as a lack (luster) argument.

Instead let's build it carefully because the strategy requires slightly more nuance (but not much more).

Why many people love feeding sentiment - engagement farming

In other words, why people love bear posting into bottom ranges, and bull posting in top ranges. This must be answered first as this explains why the crypto sentiment exists so clearly in the first place.

And the answer is simple: to farm engagement, to seem smart, and to please their audiences.

When you talk why the market topped while everyone is bearish, it is very easy to feed reasoning of why to have closed positions/sold bags at a lower price than the top (after the drop, i.e. into this bottoming range instead of at 80k instead of at 125k). That is what the audience loves to hear because they likely did too along with their engagement farming leader. Being bearish into the lows, also sounds smart, as it seems as if a plan has been playing out (yet no clear calls to back it up for, but no one tracks that anyways) and it generates lots of click, etc. etc.

These people, are engagement accounts, or occasional/frequent engagement posters (for clicks, or to push their premiums on, ad rev clicks, their constant discount sales running, or even personal feel good for attention, whatever the tricks are). 

All power to them, and no harm done. And all practices are someone's own business, none of mine. But what we can do is recognize it neatly and put it to our advantage.

So, engagement farmers often keep a bearish tone into bottoming ranges (such as candidate, 80k bottoming range right here).

And, every individual does this in their own language by the way. Which makes reading sentiment more tricky, hence why I highlight it here.

Every engagement farming individual performs a different type of analysis, or values different views. 

E.g. when sentiment is bearish, into a low, such as this low 80's low, the macro economics "expert" will tell you that the macro-economics are "looking bad". The fed "has been tightening", Trump did a bad job (whatever it all means, the news is as dubious as the speculations thrown out there themselves).

The macro investor will find reasons to say why the 4Y cycle topped for example or why macro parabola rejected, etc.

The asset class hopper will tell you to buy stocks or metals instead because they are green now as if he or she has been doing that for months, or something like that.

No matter the language, we must realize, neither of these people, perform great analysis (under the hood, using lack luster data), and just extract engagement by trying to look like a genius.

And no matter the language, because the analysis is most likely lack luster, all that matters instead, is the tone of speech, not the actual content, to use it as a sentiment read instead.

As I often mention, most (over 95%) of the views/posts/accounts on social media, are framed this way (the only-10%-of-traders/investors-make-money paradigm). And you would be surprised how many actually are just here for engagement. And it is important to classify an account or post in either an engagement post, or a proper analysis trying to call a top or bottom with actionability involved.

So case and point, how do I know if I am being helped out with useful information, or if I am more likely just being farmed?

Well, you simply ask two questions evaluating the usefulness:

Has this person made consistent actionable calls?
Has this person helped me actually make money, have I made actual gains following this person?

Critically ask these questions, and if any of these answers are no often, then you will know if this person is out to help you or just there for your engagement or there for mental masturbation.

This is important, because engagement accounts are perfect to use to our advantage to read the sentiment.  Where only actionable traders/investors (with consistent win rates - a vast vast minority), are candidates to take their analysis and execution seriously, on whatever timeframe they provide (from micro, to investing, or all sorts).

Sentiment reading: tone and timing

With awareness of engagement accounts, that leads me to my main point: track them closely, and see how their tone shifts from tops to bottoms. Not what they say, but the subtle tone in between the lines.

So again, no matter how smart or complex it or the individual seems, it doesn't matter what they say, all that matters is, the tone underneath, whether it is clearly bearish or not. And the timing of it, is it right as we are bottoming (per our chart and data analysis we present first, and are looking to confirm with sentiment).

Take notes at analysis extremes

So all you have to do, is record it (take notes).

Hence, I invite you to, take notes right now, of many accounts on X, large ones, small ones, the more, the better, of what their tone is: bearish, clearly bearish, bullish, clearly bullish (select 1 of these 4, that's it). Take notes of all of them, and how they phrase it.

Then, confirm if they are engagement accounts, by seeing if they celebrated ATH at 125k, or had a more bullish tone back then. That is direct proof of engagement accounts, as the actual behavior should have been opposite: more cautious/bearish at 125k, more bullish now.

Then, keep those notes, and add more lines to them as we spike down, you will see, of some of them, their bearish tone will peak.

Once noted, put them somewhere safe, and take them back out once we approach our beloved 112k. And you will see (I promise you), how their timeline will look a lot differently.

And once reached, again, let no words of them alter reality. You took notes, and they reflect how sentiment actually was.

If done well, you have successfully performed a sentiment read, tracking the right accounts/posts, to do so.

Summary

So in short, even if many are calling for a full bear market and they may end up being right,

It's the timing that matters, and the sentiment it reflects through the tone, not the content.

They weren't calling it at 125k on $BTC, few were, they are all doing it now.

No harm done, and excuse my harsh tone throughout this post. But sometimes, it takes harsh words to express reality.

And we can turn this reality into our benefit. As we analyzed and are calling the bottom here, it is up to us to exploit these engagement accounts as sentiment as these type of posts and accounts are invaluable for us. And it is my job to highlight this.

Their type of analysis shows up bearish during the wrong times.

It doesn't matter what type of trader or investor the person reflects to be on X, and it doesn't matter what they say exactly if they are an engagement account or have that appetite to them. To read sentiment, and detect which accounts and posts are purely or mostly for engagement, no matter how smart they seem, are the ones who have a bearish tone at the wrong time. 

Timing and Tone (T&T), to read sentiment.

Take notes of them, and their tone especially, we shall return back to this tweet when things flipped.

The engagement accounts will sound differently closer to 112k, I promise. And your notes will slowly but surely help you to detect who they are.

And I promise you, all the ones calling their bear markets now, will have put you in a way worse position to sell, then waiting out for what's after this what I call the bottom.

And, despite what many engagement farmers are causing their audiences to do, the time to sell, is not now. Not, when our analysis saids bottom with high likelihood, and not, when most engagement farmers are farming the sentiment.

Conclusion

Engagement farming accounts/posts farm engagement by posting faulty analysis, turning bearish into bottoms, bullish into tops. Their practices show up in their lack of (ability in) sharing their entries and exits, they never do present actionability.

True stakes perform analysis supporting positions, getting bullish at bottoms, bearish at tops with proper executions shared.

Engagement accounts and posts support sentiment, true stakes accounts support analysis.

Use this to your advantage to read sentiment.

Disclaimer

This post is not directed at anyone specifically and is purely written for educational purposes.

There is no room for emotion and/or beef in trading and investing. Keeping it calm, and factual.

Enjoy. And once our current sentiment read is complete, you will be one step closer to understanding it.

Actionable and live teaching (aimed to be) presented here.

$BTC 

4 year cycles, why the top is not in necessarily, and why bears are overconfident right here, one final hint

Alright, giving one more hint about the heated argument currently going on, of the large, large majority ever so confidently calling the top on $BTC now just because November has been the 35th month of this cycle since the low, and because we always have topped around month 35 or 36 so far, and for some reason, that is why it should top again, "guaranteed".

That, is what everyone is saying today into this 80k low. (And no, they didn't say it at the 125k top, so let's lock that emotional aspect in our minds too).

If your belief is that the top is in now, all power to you. And you could very well be right. And I respect your view.

From a data analysis perspective, it is absolutely ludicrous how much confidence people put behind that single idea.

More-over, how much confidence is placed behind one idea consisting of just 3 historic data points. Not the first time we see this type of show on here, so let's approach this a bit more carefully.

If you are serious about investing, you know how I always go on about using more than just 3 data points. 7 should be the least, ideally from a few low-correlated sources.

How do we get more data points ? We simply look one tiny step beyond crypto to find more clues.

Finding the next clue...

... is very simple. Stepping outside of crypto indeed, let's take $BTC's bigger brother, gold for example.

Before I go further, I know stepping outside of crypto is sometimes considered a crime on CT. I apologize for the non crypto post. Personally, I enjoy it as much as crypto. Crypto is just easy as opinions are so strong about it which makes sentiment very easily readable, much easier than other asset classes.

On top, believe it or not, crypto cycles move just like commodity cycles, as both are the purest form of tradeable assets, tied the least to one specific economy (no specific country created gold, nor $BTC).

So let's remove our crypto hats for a bit, and put on our commodity hats, where data is a lot richer as commodities have been around for decades.

The data

Gold, just like $BTC, moves in 4 year cycles, but has more resolution at half pace, so essentially, it moves in 8 year cycles. Reasons why this is, I choose to not explain for now, maybe for another tweet. But just keep in mind that moving in 1 8 year cycle is the same as moving in 2 4 year cycles. Cycles are intertwined.

So on the 2 month chart, that means, the cycles play out just like $BTC.

On the chart below, clearly visible indeed. Every single low is placed around that 48 candle count mark on the 2M (2 monthly), just like how $BTC's low is placed around that 48 candle mark count on the M (monthly) chart.

But on gold, we can clearly see, how the top is not reliably placed the 35th or 36th month, as how $BTC has.

Indeed, sometimes, the top can be as early as candle 17, but sometimes, it can be as late as 42.

If $BTC were to top at candle count 42 right now, it would go up all the way until May.

Not saying it will, but just giving you the idea, that going all in on the idea that we topped in November, just because it was month 36, is like playing roulette, gambling on number 36, while the number could still end up between 36-42.

To find the top, we use other data, that is a story for another time.

But I just wanted to highlight that indeed, the 4 year cycle works well, extremely well, but it only works well from bottom to bottom. Using it to call tops, is wrong, putting your money on that, is risky, and using it as a sole thesis to call a top, especially on an asset class that only has placed 3 tops in history so far, is ridiculous at least according to my risk management. 

Hope you enjoyed this tweet. Just wanted to get it out there because I felt like it was a necessity, with all the misinformation out there nowadays.

Yes, I am bullish, for different reasons. For the right reasons. And IMO bears using this as an argument, are bearish for the wrong reasons.

Summary

Using November as a top signal, purely because it is the 35th month of the cycle, and purely because it happened 3 times before, is using a limited amount of data to support an overconfident thesis. Like gambling all in on throwing 6 with a dice, betting the top will be November is ludicrous risk management.

Just looking a tiny bit beyond crypto, proves that already, as the gold chart speaks for itself.

Without saying any more, risk forms I am sharing too much at this point, so this post is the last one on 4 year cycle talk.

Enjoy, I am out and back to trading.

tweets.text:
$BTC - is the bear market here?

Why using MA's is essentially gambling.

Alright, the is about the 7th time I get tagged of someone telling me the following:

"We closed below the 50W MA and are far below it, so the bear market started".

Okay, I like your thinking. Using actual data to predict price.

However, have you thoroughly fact checked this data? Who brought you to the idea, did you come up with this yourself?

All power to you, regardless of the answer, but just a simple check, can help you very far.

So I will quickly present you here why using MA's is something only "chartists" do, but has 0 use in trading as it is essentially gambling.

Indeed, I will simply and effectively show you how, it has no merit to use a random average price of the x most recent candle closes, as a metric whether price will go down or up.

The data

MA's are broad, so let's use something truly relevant right now as an example. Since so so many people are confidently and loudly preparing for the bear market, almost as if they have their limit orders ready to buy $BTC at 50k/40k/30k... wouldn't it be great to present how most of the data I have to debunk time after time (the one of the 50 W MA), is a pure myth of fairy dust...

So as mentioned, the argument goes: Astro, we closed below the 50 W MA and are significantly below it, that has "always" been a bear market trigger.

Well, let's check, and let's check properly (non cherry picked).

On the chart below, I highlighted every single weekly swing low that has formed each time $BTC fell under the 50 WMA. And I did that throughout its entire history (no cherry picking)

What's a swing low? It's per classic institutional definition: a candle where the low of the candle to the left and right are both higher than the candle itself. Indeed, the very definition of a low, in its most simple and fundamental form.

To eliminate even more noise, I only counted the swing lows where also a candle close below the 50 W MA has been placed (otherwise, a wick into the 50W MA, would also be counted as a bottom, and the data would look even less favorable for the bear market callers here, so, I choose your side wherever I can).

The times of the first weekly swing lows after which $BTC went from closing above to closing below the 50 W MA are:

➡️17 Oct 2011
➡️18 Aug 2014
➡️18 Jun 2018
➡️(25 Nov 2019)
➡️9 Mar 2020
➡️19 Jul 2020
➡️13 Dec 2021

And today:

➡️17 Nov 2025

For each of the occasions, price headed lower, 3 out of 6 times. And 3 out of 6 times, price printed the absolute bottom.

Yes, I left out 25 Nov 2019 (covid crash, if it didn't happen, it would have been a bottom, otherwise, technically price heading lower, although it went so quick, that it is hard to call it a prolonged bear market, so let's skip it. The results do not change much).

So in essence, if you are using this as a sole argument to call whether the bear market is in or not, then you are essentially betting your money on a coinflip i.e. you are gambling.

The problem with MA's

I don't really have an issue with MA's. They can be useful, but they are purely descriptive. So, they are nice to see on charts, and "chartists" often use them to describe price:

"Price is below the MA, price is above the MA, price is far below the MA, price is far above the MA"

But they are not predictive.

If price is "far" below the MA, it doesn't mean price will perform a mean reversion => followed by a reversal i.e. a bottom

Or a mean reversion => followed by continuation lower

As I have just shown with this example. To use them whether they have the power to call a bear market or not, is a complete toss-up.

And that is because of their core problem: they carry no logic. They are simply the average price of the most recent x candles. No one cares what that price is. Institutions don't care, the trend doesn't care, the macro economics don't care, the whales don't care, no one cares.

If a trend is "riding" the 20 ma, that is just a description of the steepness of the trend. If the trend changes, then all the 20 ma buyers will get rekt.

If the trend steepens even ever so slightly, then the 20 ma buyers will all get front run and have to fomo in higher.

They just describe the steepness of the trend, they don't define the trend, and the same is true for bear markets, they don't define bear markets (or bull markets either).

Conclusion

The 50 MA, and MA's in general, have no statistical power (not even negatively i.e. in counter sense), nor do they care any logic. They are completely descriptive, and completely random in predictive power.

To call whether the bear market has started, or we just printed another bull market bottom, it's best to use other, more logical and statistically powerful data.

Let this be clear. IMO anyone using MA's should just be classified as a chartist with no implication on stakes. Or he or she is just trying to describe price and has no ability to predict price, at least not using those metrics.

So all power to them, but best not to mix both up, even if said influencer tells you how "perfectly" price bounced off his or her ma. Great, but not great for consistently being successful in this game.

Successful trading and investing is just as much about using the right data, as avoiding the wrong data.

Especially the latter, so here is another piece to your puzzle of mastery.

Take it, or leave it.

This is just my view.

It's up to you if you believe it.

tweets.text:
$BTC

Full analysis, plan and why it's not worth to be overly bearish, nor overly bullish either

Local lows (75.3k) are unsafe, but I don't expect a deep bear market.

Good morning.

As you all know, my bullish bias established in the 80-85k range, where I expected the range to reach 95k and especially 112k, has just been invalidated. It held 11 weeks, we got a 20% move, got 95k move. From it, had a few wins (8), but also 2 losses I took myself (and 3 suggested trades), so let's count it as 3.

Two losses defly from being too confident in 112k from the 80-85k range. Still confident in that level, but not from a trading perspective worth mentioning.

So 3 losses, 8 wins certainly not ideal and below my standards/usual record, I made some clear mistakes as well as no readiness for unclear weekend-macro events etc.

I certainly expected this bias to hold for longer and price going higher, but ah well.

About my PnL throughout this range, it started out really well, of course as many know, but then ended up giving a large amount of it back unfortunately.

Also wish I sold a lot more of my spot positions at 125k, as you know only posted to sell a tiny amount at 125k, same for $ETH at 5k. And of course, the first compounds of spot at 84k we aimed to sell at 112k, I also still hold and are below entry (for now).

Plan next

During times like this, draw boarding needs to be heavier as plan didn't work out. So I'm exactly sharing here what my plan is next, what I will do with my positions (action = key), and what type of trades (long or short) I am looking for as well as where, giving a deep summary and comments on thought process (which is key).

As you know, I like to be thorough, one line doesn't define a trade, only a thorough system does especially now after taking some losses. And only the thorough reader gets access to my full plan.

Top to bottom

On big drawboarding sessions, always going from top to bottom (high timeframe then to lower timeframe).

On the very high cyclical timeframe, I already expressed how, if my bias would fail and we close below 81k (not yet done but let's expect it for now), it's going somewhat lower, but it's not going to be a deep bear market.

I drew the next purple POI (as per usual, purple weekly POI = similar style to every weekly low I called in the past) where I expect price to at least put in a serious countertrend rally from. To 112k? I'll get to that in later posts, not relevant right now.

But it will be a "bottom" worth buying long timeframe on local confirmations

The purple POI is quite a way below us but it indeed is not a classic -80% bear market, only 50% off the all time high. Another reason why I wasn't all too bearish high timeframe as it wasn't as important. I'm still wrong of course but as long as longs are exited, it's all fine.

This worst case (but now turning likely) case of scenario is what I quietly once thought about would be the worst if I was wrong and we topped 125k, so here it is, the devils verdict I didn't but any weight on.

I don't guarantee it yet, like I said, it's not entirely clear where I think the market will go next, so very much an if this, then that type of post here, with a worst case scenario (purple) in mind, but key to have for our long term (spot BTC, alts on confirmation only) thoughts.

Moving down a timeframe (H6/H12, where my edge is focused and where I trade actively), 

We have weekend lows, as well as favourable cyclical timing for lower (cycle not done yet, more on that later).

To our disadvantage unfortunately, execution was bad on that , but level worked very well as the one pivot deciding which way the 80-85k value area would break, the value area is still the same so I still have it on the chart.

We also still have the 90.8k key level we pointed out which still held itself very strongly.

To our disadvantage unfortunately, execution was bad on that as you know, but level worked very well as the one pivot deciding which way the 80-85k value area would break, the value area is still the same so I still have it on the chart.

My actions

So, actions follow naturally from plan here, giving both spot and trade actions

Positional actions (spot multi-day/weekly timeframe)

Since my bullish bias is invalidated, I am naturally no longer actively looking for longs. But also because I don't expect a deep bear market, I am not selling any spot here, I am in 80% in here, avg entry 34k, which used to be 21.5k (I'm sure many remember this post), but due to the recent ads at 84k 11 weeks ago, has gone up of course..

That's still a comfy entry, if you have a similar entry (I assume the minority I only had about 5k followers or so back at our $BTC 21.5k call. So I can already hear you: "what if I only bought 84k spot and I didn't have any before?"

In that case, if you are heavily allocated, I would try to sell some (half) right now and especially getting closer to 90.8k (gradual but aggressive selling)

I don't think selling all makes sense, given my expectations of not receiving much worse than a 50% drawdown at worst, and 84k already being down 30% from ath, are still decent entries.

But it's good to keep a large portion open for the purple below to correct overall entry and position better for the next bull run.

Swing trade actions (futures)

Per last $BTC post, no longer exposed in perps, and bullish bias invalidated. I am not overly bearish as is clear from the chart, but shifted neutral. That means looking for a range for me to establish that neutral range and get back to trading it as well.

Again not entirely clear where the range will form yet. But happy to trade it as we go. Not from the long side for now, but only from the short side, as I indeed see weekend lows get cleared and they also are defined weak on the TPO.

But I'm not shorting from right here, rather closer to 90.8k (our key pivot/reclaim) for better RR as well as closing CME gap first i.e. 84k, only then targeting weekend lows.

What if we go full moon (after taking weekend lows)?

It's always possible, and doing so before hitting purple is of course also possible. But I don't see it likely at all before hitting weekend lows first, and even after, we very likely clear out the Mar-May lows first, and that already puts us close to purple, which should be deemed a magnet on proximity for demand and spread manipulation reasons.

If it does happen though, I will gladly sell spot at 112k, the still existing magnet, but then expect a large downswing which I will look to short for a large move down.

So in short, only looking for shorts at the moment. $BTC trends (down in this case) can extend, there still is money there, so that's what I look to grab, whilst keeping in mind high timeframe the bottom is likely far closer than many think (still going somewhat against the sentiment of this cycle playing out like 2022 and this range leading us all the way to 30k).

Don't think so, likely bottoming much higher, but not yet and closer to the middle of the year.

Trade entries will be shared live as always (which is key), and I always look to confirm with local order flow and will comment on it.

Summary;TLDR

In short, BTC broke my bullish bias, which I didn't deem likely, but here it is.

This means I am not bullish for a while.

I am not overly bearish either high timeframe as just expressed as I don't see lower than 60k, which isn't worth being bearish for, can't make much from selling spot in full and buying back lower, that's too risky.

Instead just looking to swing trade, with taking a short if we hit CME close first, targeting weekend lows.

If weekend lows are hit first, I will not be looking to long, at least not with heavy confirmation first.

Going full moon is also possible right after clearing weekend lows, but I don't see that likely at all here after bullish bias invalidation.

That is my plan for now, plus actions. Backed by price action, range theory, cyclical analysis, liquidity arrangement and my own core edge.

So  all-in-all, not too bad to hold spot through, which is why I am holding it.

Key is to get in the right trades, and up the win rate again from the recent 8/11 wins (=72%) without forcing it.

Final disclaimers

I never guarantee 100% win rate. But I do always aim making (very good) money if risk managed well.

I do know it's joyful going all in because you found me not missing for a long period on trades in a recent time right after you found me such as some dm's.

But do risk manage, a good start is taking the same size on every trade. Yes, some of those dm's did proceed of people being liquidated because of my last 2/3 trades. But then I asked what size they took and it was 4 times higher than the wins I posted as they gained confidence in my streak. Not logical as most trades were exited before even hitting -1R and not held in long drawdown. Always same size (scaled to timeframe is the healthiest check.

Enjoy the analysis, plan and comments on risk management.

Set new lows during the weekend, getting out on this 81.3k  local bounce and took the loss for now

Exited longs for now. Looked all good Yesterday until we received this weekend drop.

Although we likely close CME gap close to 84k, IMO, not worth holding this long through as weekends are unpredictable when they trend like this. Every drop lower sets the weekend low lower and weekend lows here have a high chance of being taken out next week.

Puts the long and also the bias at risk so getting out here is key to limit losses.

As much as it was my job to show you where and how to exit on the 8 wins we had recently on the backbone of the bullish bias throughout this range, now it's also equally much my job to show you how to do it when losses occur, as well as openly admit when my idea is wrong.

So as promised, exiting the long here and taking a few steps back on leverage, not thinking about any trade soon.

Yes, range low sweep is possible, and yes, we could absolutely reverse all of it.

But we are in an illiquid weekend environment during a monthly close and with uncertainty of macro news (whether it will happen or not is unclear).

Going to sit aside here, just stay in spot and let the market give some serious confirmation first before going long again.

I apologize for the idea being wrong, but range breakdown potential especially with early signs during the weekend = simply admitting it's wrong.

As promised and per discipline, that is also when I have to go at least towards neutral and wait for a serious structure shift before thinking about long again.

As a final note, in the case of the bias being wrong, I did say it wouldn't be worth shorting like we did in 2022 aiming for -80% bear market, so just pointing out that waiting out is better than getting arrogant high timeframe shorting here.

So along with that, I wouldn't fear a deep drop.

But at least a neutral view is key as well as just getting out.

$BTC longs

Still around entry, de-risked half here, looking to re-enter after gov shutdown day is done.

Quick updates, thoughts and detailed plan further

Entered a $BTC long Yesterday and since, $BTC went up about 1,200 pts from entry, dropped below 1,800 pts below and is currently back around entry (just 250 pts under).

Good news first: we have a monthly OHLC on Jan with high and low of Dec taken which has a high chance of closing above Dec low (83.7 k), and this Feb likely shapes up bullish.

Less ideal news: we have to get through the monthly close first upon gov shutdown and the first reaction up was suboptimal.

Today (Friday) is the time to close above though since weekend volatility is likely continuing to be low (we are in a range).

So about the less ideal news of the gov shutting down, happening Tomorrow. I don't like to blame the news, instead I have templates for all types to deal with it. But for this event, currently, it's not fully clear as I have few for such events.

Even worse is that it happens on the weekend which can create weekend lows.

So action wise, that means holding the long until the end of Today, if it doesn't close above 83.7k or close to that, I'll likely exit early to limit loss due to this edge case (be on lookout for my post at that time). Otherwise, hold for longer as upon gov shutdown, uncertainty is over and price rises on top of bullish bias and hopefully Friday has at least a wick.

But if we close this daily below Dec low, I suspect we clear the 81k low upon news release (which is common). It does mean upon news that it would be manipulation, likely would create weekend lows so we likely range there until next week, then clear them, or still close weekly below 81k and clear it next week (and close back above).

It would be the absolute worst case whilst still holding the bullish bias.

Not going to long aggressively and immediately in that case, nor hold the long even if it's the best price. So in that case, will just hold spot which is still valid to hold.

After the weekly close, re-evaluate for longs and after clearing potential weekend lows, re-evaluate for spot.

Not doomsday prepping any further, that's just if gov shutdown turns out badly. Other than that, price did follow the drawn out plan so far, so hopefully, it bounces. I can't really tell as again order flow is not fully clear for now. 

But risk will be limited as de-risked half here and look to exit early indeed upon Today's close potentially.

After all is said and done, Feb has set up to be bullish, hence my subbornness here, also because we haven't closed any weekly below 81k yet.

All other scenarios (not drawn) and long and bias need to be reassed. Hence, if idea is wrong = get out of trade and hence my SL placement to account for both if I decide to not exit early.

Hope these details are clear. Apologize for slightly higher complexity than usual, but need to treat longs sensibly as discussed last posts even if our bias played out confidently for 10 weeks so far. 

Do not read these details as a lack of conviction, to the contrary, I still have it in full for this trade, again, price is following my line to the exact dollar. 

But I won't celebrate it until the deal is done. So meanwhile just want to give you these details to show you how I think, also to prepare you and not feel left out/know what to do in any scenario.

As always, the importance is in the details, not in vague calls.

One of the most misunderstood concepts in markets:

Price doesn't need sellers to move down or buyers to move up.

Conceptually, if the lowest asker in $BTC asks 97100, and the second lowest asker, asks 99000.

And the lowest asker decides to no longer sell his/her $BTC, and removes asks, then price succesfully moved up without anyone buying or selling.

Not buying or selling, instead this, determines 90% of the market's price movement and is called market making.

The act of it moves price, and it is driven as a counter of generic sentiment which in turn is a product of cyclical advance.

tweets.text:
$BTC - what creates consistent investing/trading results.

Comes down to one very simple sentence: establish the bias we are in right now first (confirm if right or frame doubt if maybe wrong using sentiment), then find a trade based on that.

You see faults and cracks of avoiding this absolutely foundational rule all the time. Especially now, but also during the 80-85k range as we saw.

People calling for the bear market back in the 80-85k range, people still shorting this breakout and powerful high volume green now.

They are faults because succesful trading/investing comes down to knowing (anticipating) the bias in present time.

That's it. Right now, not sometime in the future, not in the past (in hindsight). What matters is now and the very mext move.

The very next move from the 80-85k range was not down (and so, it made absolutely no sense to call for a bear market even if true right there, because the timing was off). The right post wasn't "the bear market started". That is lazy and complacent. Anyone who read the market deeply and put in the hours, knew the right call was "another bottom just formed, we'll see later where it ends"

And so the bias was up, not down. And that is all that mattered.

Even if you call for a bearish retest. Well then, you have a bullish bias until complete, don't you?

Shorting before a bearish retest gets you rekt, as we have been seeing over and over.

So how do you get the right bias?

You must at all times know four things:

1️⃣Are we in a range?
If yes: bias = range
2️⃣Which way will it break
3️⃣Will it break soon? When will it break? (And will we start trending)
4️⃣If in a trend, when will it end?

Knowing these four, and you will know exactly when to trade the range (if 1️⃣ = yes and 3️⃣= no), when to trade the trend (if 3️⃣= yes and 2️⃣= known) and when the trend will end again (4️⃣).

That's all it takes to know the bias (range, trend up, trend down, yes, there are 3 biases, not 2)

We're seeing so much ignorance. Good low timeframe traders eating loss after loss because they found good entries in the range but their trades get chewed up now that we are in an uptrend (right after we entered our high timeframe long about 1 month ago at 85.2k).

And so they didn't see the uptrend coming.

We're still seeing those same faults occur. Continued shorts being rekt or selling being regretted.

Research bias first. Then research your entry.

And of course to find the right bias, use the right metrics and tools.

Wont disclose how right now nor here.

But what I just wrote, is the framework. Even the framework isn't understood on X right now.

And it never has been.

Research bias first, entry second. Not the other way around.

We just scored a nice move, from bottom, to local top (so far). That's also our fifth win in a row locked, all called out live...

You may feel good now, and confident, and that's good. In fact it's exactly my goal to give you that confidence and give you the feeling that the trading/investing dream is real.

Because it is very real, it is as real as it gets. We scored all of it for the world to see, all you had to do was copy it.

The next challenge, comes after the move. After such big move, the market often chops, and it does so very efficiently.

It does that to:

A/ Try to extract liquidity from the ones who missed it (around 30% of the liquidity at the moment), they vulnerable to fomo, a strong emotion in the human nervous system.

B/ Try to induce revenge trading of the ones who were (spot hedged or normal) short, who force to make it back (60% of the liquidity at the moment), vulnerable to revenge trading (anger is different to fomo, but another strong emotion).

C/ To try and extract the liquidity of the confident trader who just won (10% of the liquidity at the moment), the least vulnerable, but regret is still a strong emotion. So only if you humbly partialed e.g. at my level of 69k, you are safe.

So regardless who you are, chop after a big move is beneficial for liquidity extraction.

Having accurate targets and taking big partials right on those targets, and already locking in the win at exactly 69k, is what prevents you from trying to make any moves now even if you have won, since you are still in a trade.

Secondly, you won't be stressed on this pullback either since you already acted on TP'ing 69k.

This is why I make the move of a partial TP at the right level.

It makes trading almost completely stress free, and limits mistakes.

That's practice versus reality.

"Chartists" (who just quote old calls that "played out"), do not know about this type of reality.

They only draw (beautiful) bridges, but have no idea if it will collapse after x years due to conditions over time (corrosion).

Trading > charting, for many many reasons.

I am here to help you through the journey to freedom, enjoy it.
