Great point. You mentioned the essence of shaping edge.

Edge which works (properly) on every timeframe is rare despite being claimed so with many "one model traders". But neither is it a requirement.

Good confluence just needs to show profitability on at least one timeframe you want to use it on, over the entire history (or as far back as possible). Even if its slightly, before it can be considered a confluence, and not noise.

The entire history is a requirement to make sure all conditions are covered. Because if it only works in "certain conditions", then the edge is defining the conditions, not the item itself.

For example, why use an MA to trade mean reversions (back to the MA when extended), if you can just draw a range itself and trade that. Then the MA's are noise, (which adds to paralysis by analysis).

Simply knowing the fact the market will range, is the only edge.

So I'm closing the trade here (for 80%). Why 80% and not full? Because my plan remains and thus keeping small leftovers is an execution strategy which keeps you engaged to your plan of execution.

In reality, it actually drifts you out of tune with the market and makes you prone to fomo for longs or shorts (traders biggest enemy). So keeping small leftovers helps you stay engaged.

Rotating profits again into another long.

Alright, market rejected quite accurately off our institutional level announced Yesterday and TP level.

Had some question as to "why I TP'd so aggressively"

Aside from my answers, I said the TP is not an easy one, admittedly. But the market has now answered that question for us.

Per announcement I just made, I want to long again. So I rotated Yesterday's profits back into a fresh long here, with 66k remaining my directional level.

As I indeed still expect 66k. With the smooth high timeframe lows at 59k taken out now, we can increase the distance and conviction on the long again.

Yes, it is still a downtrend. Yes, I am still "longing a downtrend". Yes, "shorting would have been better". 

But you're talking in hindsight. "trading the trend" is hindsight talk. You catch the long before that, which is what we are doing.

No prediction, by definition, is ever built on hindsight.

But yes to those: I have indeed been longing the downtrend from 62.xk and below and "I should have kept my short from 67k open instead". If I could explain to the novice who don't actively trade this market yet in two lines why following a plan is more important than trying to be perfect and squeeze every penny, I would. But there's no time and I'm trying to get this post out there as fast as possible at this important hourly range low area here.

The plan is since 62.x k to look for longs and longs only, even if the hindsight answer is countertrend.

And I do apologize for the fast action scalp-like trades and early TP'd according to our local levels and reaction. I also do promise 66k is still coming.

Just keep in mind it won't be in a straight line, it won't be "Tomorrow" with a fast magical rocket-like move. It will be eventually and is a very profitable distance away from here.

Confluences for this long are (amongst others): in high timeframe zone, htf golden & silver zone, vPOC, 66k magnet above, poor highs at 65.5k, high timeframe spot order flow support, and sentiment wise, many calling for sub 50k.

Makes me continue the long position, just like before. Rinse and repeat.

Biases:

➡️Weekly: bullish. I think we bottom 60k and the bears are wrong.
➡️Daily: I think we range, range high: our 67k short level. Range low: our 60k region long level(s).
➡️Hourly: shifting bullish. Called out how we range. We are now at range low and I think we reach higher again.

Current long leverage: 0.53x (macro bottom potential, not a time to go 4x or + like mindless gamblers).

Enjoy, let's see if we can get another W and hopefully a big one to 66k. I do expect so.

$btc: my next move, revealed

Fully closed shorts IV, and started flipping it into a long. Can we get 5 wins in a row?

Alright! There it is, the next trade has arrived.

For me, it is time to take a long.

Long, you said Astro? What about the FOMC reversal, has it finished? What does that mean for our shorts?

Keep reading.

The type of long

It's an intraweek long, a long to complete the weekly move. That's still a swing trade, but it means all liquidity left during the week needs to be cleared.

Why a long? Why ignore the remainder of the FOMC reversal?

Yes FOMC reversal is still at play, and our 7% minimal drawdown still isn't finished.

But you have to keep in mind, that we called the FOMC reversal from 66.3k, where we entered short, and we already dropped 6.3%+ from the high.

If you think you can get away with just using 1 confluence all the time, and make money consistently, you will get wrecked instead.

Not always financially, but at the very least emotionally, which propagates into financial ruin regardless.

And that's because when a move starts to get close to completion, bounces against the move start to become more violent. That's again the trapping mechanism at work trapping big liquidity before reaching big liquidity.

So what's the move to finish the week? It's the untouched weekly open and the liquidity left during the course of the week.

That's almost a 2000 points move at least, lots of money to be made.

So what about our shorts?

It's simple, given the FOMC reversal is coming to an end for its initial move, it's no longer beneficial to hold the aggressive short (short IV). But it still makes sense to hold short III, because that's the top short, that's the one that should be closed only when most of the confluences fully confirm the FOMC reversal is over, not the case yet.

So in summary, the plan is simple:

➡️We have developed the bulk of the FOMC reversal move down
➡️The weekly move is still unfinished, likely to complete this week possibly all the way into next week.
➡️Close short VI, flip it into a long.

TLDR;
➡️Fully close aggressive short IV
➡️Flip into new long position

Why we countertrend shorted above 66k - confluence 5 - the sentiment.

The fifth confluence is quite simple, of how there was a remarkable sentiment shift from below 60k, loudly expressed, to above 66k, where it again became loudly expressed in the opposite direction.

How to find out? The ones who took note of the typical bear post engagement farming posts, both blatant and more encrypted in "smart analysis" form, know.

I told you below 60k to take note of those posts and who is behind it, and then see who shifts tone and when. Above 66k, it happened.

Why below 60k and why the shift above 66k?

Because at both ends, a significant low got taken out, so a lot of liquidity gets generated that way in form of panic selling, in lockstep with how their favourite influencer suddenly talks again about how the bear market "is here, told you so" below 60k, all for just a move of a couple % lower below 60k. And suddenly now about how a bottom has formed, or "rally in July".

So whatever the excuse may be each time, it's not about the content, but the overall tone and timing of the post.

We hinted to take track of those type of posts and frequency, and (most of) those same patterns of ports started repeatedly appearing above 66k how they told you July would rally, how the bottom is suddenly in now convincingly, and how their masterplan will play out.

Again, not the content that matters, but the tone and timing of the post.

When reading sentiment, always look at who, timing and tone, to gather a picture.

That's not to be directed at anyone, but just the sheer reality of this game, we like to use to confirm our trade entries.

A good trade is generally an unpopular trade, or, a more popular trade at a less popular time (leaving the popular opinion side lined).

That's sentiment reading in a nutshell.

And no, I'm not naming any names of accounts I track. That's confidential, and this is not directed at anyone. The idea is clear, the idea I use to make money more confidently. And that's more than enough to set you on your way.

Why we countertrend shorted above 66k - confluence 1

Alright, as promised, after sharing the entry which is already 3 hours ago, I would share one by one why I am considering this countertrend short after hitting our major major target, 66k.

In the post itself, I have given all reasons, but I promised to lay them out with the respective charts, one by one.

Not something I can share in one post, since, as many of you know, my trades aren't just based on one chart or idea, they are a full construct and detailed plan of a lot of strong confluences to get to the full idea, the golden standard before even considering entering the market, especially on a countertrend trade.

Here is one of them, it's the FOMC reversal. As many of you may already know, and as I am also known for, for sharing this analysis in the past many times.

In fact, almost every time, days before FOMC comes around, I shared this analysis, with the announcement of "FOMC is happening IMO", or, on the rare occasion "we may see FOMC continuation this time, as shared in October/November 2024.

Why days before? 

Because the market tends to reverse before the FOMC meeting, not during or after.

Like clockwork, where the masses anticipate a "large move" after the meeting, exit their trades (at the worst times), to "stay safe", the market has already reversed.

That's the FOMC reversal in a nutshell. It works with 90%+ accuracy, and with another meeting coming up on the 29th of July, we have another FOMC reversal idea coming up, of price reversing the uptrend back down.

For how much of a move and how long you ask? That's an analysis for another time, and just using this analysis for that, the targets, is not sufficient.

And that brings us back full circle, as to why I never base my trades off of just one analysis. FOMC reversal is a direction and a mild onset of an entry idea, not a target, not a full trade framework.

But it's strong confluence to a rather great swing of direction, one that almost always makes you money.

And as a full time trader, that's all that matters, in my world.

Context first, for the ones who are new, but also the ones who have been around, context matters a lot.

The best practice before setting expectations to the future, is to refer to recent past first on all timeframes. Context matters. Especially when a major target such as 66k hits. How it hits, changes the meaning of it hitting.

Recently, we ranged for a very long time sub 60k, and had a slow move up close to 66k, not hitting it, followed by a final quick burst from sub 63k (62.5k) to finally going north of 66k.

To get there was a process, lots of traps formed, even all the way up to the final move on July 15th which fell just shy of 66k. We shorted it back to the NYO pico low, our infamous cat and mouse game of recent past.

We trapped the mouse and brought home 66k. It secured us two wins in a row again, with this trade, we are aiming to get a third win in a row for obvious reasons (NFA).

Overall, what just happened, and the entire move to 60k, is classic major liquidity play, of setting traps until finally hitting a major liquidity level.

Major liquidity targets don't get hit, they are reached in the form of a trap first, before clearance so this indeed confirms that 66k+ was a major liquidity target.

And the final move to it, was a rather swift move. That is our context, and already gives clues to what next.

More context, is the fact that July has grabbed June's low, before reaching higher, it hasn't done it without grabbing June's low, which tells us the intent of July's end of month PA is different, it tells us a weaker end than if June's low wasn't taken, and it tells us June's midpoint (66k) is also of more importance than if June's low wasn't taken. That's added confluence to the expectations of July's end.

So overall, context gives us reasons to at the very least, not be overly bullish here north 66k+. Is it a short position? Not yet. Can't just trade on "vibes" and context alone. We're going deeper.

Biases

Next, are biases. Are they still the same? What are my directional expectations?

Weekly bias

My weekly bias remains: 60k region is the bottom, I have been and still think the bears are wrong, and this move to 66k+ only solidified the 60k region as a bottom, where the daily range extends and builds more liquidity. So I still think we don't see sub 50k, that remains.

It not changing, is only logical, a daily target hitting, doesn't mean a weekly bias changes, it means at most, a daily bias changes if all conditions of the target hitting fulfil.

Daily bias

And since it has, and since this was a major target, my daily bias indeed now has changed. It's no longer bullish, because indeed my daily target of 66k has been hit.

It's cautiously bearish now. I say cautiously, and that's a keyword, because we are in a weekly regime which imo bottoms us out. Which means that my bias isn't permanently bearish here on the daily timeframe nor is it bearish for a long time. It's cautiously or "countertrend" bearish. A weekly bottoming regime is not a time to attach a heavy bearish bias on the daily against the trend, and it explains why this isn't a heavy short either, it's a lighter one.

And that positioning here, goes in lockstep with the mindset "don't gamble away your profits straight away". We just scored major gains at 66k closing 3 longs at the same time (except runners), no need to gamble them away with large overly confident positions.

Hourly bias

Of less importance, but this bias can help local impatience. My bias locally, is still a range/slow pa here. Which supports why I think there is still time for this move to play out.

Magnets

Next, are magnets. They need to support our bias. Weekly magnets: none below. Last one was 60k, that's cleared, a long time ago already (since Feb).

Daily magnets are present: we have poor lows on the TPO charts, both locally and still lingering in the sub 63k region as well. Keeping in mind, poor lows on their own, not a guaranteed magnet, especially not in a weekly bottoming regime, but they ad to the overall confidence.

Finally, the weekly open untapped, you already know what that means.

Further confluences and timing

Furthermore, we are in the lower high region (LH region) of June 15th high, classic place to expect rotations to occur.

Added to that, we have mmd with $eth, I'm also going to leave no further comment to what that means, long term followers know, just ask them in the comments.

And finally, we have FOMC meeting to the 29th of July. Also no need to express what that means. Type in FOMC reversal in my post history search function, and you know.

Summary

In short, I went short here , no pun intended. We just hit our major 66k liquidity target, the target we have waited for, for a very long time.

The way we reached it, combined with the confluences, which are quite a few, are enough to expect some digestion of the move up that just happened.

We are trying to capture that. Not in an ultra bearish way, but in a cautious, against the trend way, with still enough potential to make good money type of way.

So keep in mind, the decision of this trade is on the edge. Not every predicted/expected move should be traded. Some aren't worth it since they have lower tail reward. There are no guarantees, and I sometimes get it wrong too. This is one of them. Although FOMC reversal can offer bigger moves, and $eth mmd can offer resistance longer than people are confident on.

So label this very much as a countertrend short attempt, one worth taking. And adjust your size to what your tolerance suggest is good for countertrend plays like this.

Enjoy, plan is given, outlines are clear, and over time, I will create more posts, reminders and also sentiment reads supporting this countertrend thesis.

But for now, I just want to pioneer this pullback idea, in case we get copied or ideas get pushed around, to have this as a reference to be "the first", etc etc.

Per rule of credit where due, but also because being prepared early is good. Being prepared early is important.

Macro (Weekly/monthly): bullish
Daily timeframes (positional): no longer bullish

Extensive post is below. But here's a short version/quick recap if you missed the bottom/breakout and genuinely feel frozen out:

🥇 First priority: don't lose money.
Don't revenge short, don't short "back to your entry", and don't stay stubbornly bearish just because you missed the move.

🥈 Accept the conditions changed.
We're trending up. That doesn't mean straight up, it means HH → HL → HH → HL. Flip the switch from trying to fade everything to understanding you're in a buyers market.

🥉 Then focus on buying dips, not chasing local tops.
You don't need insanely complex TA for this. Support/resistance, the right EMA, liquidation flushes, simple TA works when you correctly understand the market conditions.

Effective TA can be very easy, but understanding the conditions of the market is hard m yet only the latter makes the former work.

Buy dips with conviction, let price move away, then manage profit accordingly.

If leveraged, take significant exposure off before the next expected flush. If spot, focus more on slowly selling into the eventual overall market top.

You haven't missed the opportunity to make money.

You're simply dealing with different conditions now imo.

Money-making potential in a market never ends.

An imo timely reminder.

Alright, we had our period of boredom finish loudly and clearly now with a strong green weekly candle. That shifts the phase a bit further now, which, as expressed, is a strong breakout not to be faded.

That strong breakout - the way bitcoin does it - is to leave people sidelined.

That is why, after taking the loss on the shorts pre breakout, we, on top of the spot bags we bulk bought, went long after the breakout and what typically happens next sentiment wise is the market trying to freeze out most people indeed.

By that I mean the ones that "DCA'd the bottom" (but probably only entered with insignificant size. Because who ever finishes "DCA-ing".

Furthermore, it tries to sideline the ones that were short, but even the ones that TP'd long too early, or that ones that simply left crypto and where the first waves are considering coming back slowly.

Essentially, the market tries to sideline everyone unaware of breakout scenarios, unaware of the sentiment, and unaware how to position on that without missing out.

Because missing out does cost. It's the whole point fomo exists. Not to be that person, but no one ever said they didn't mind missing bitcoin back when it was sub 1$. Missing out can be costly, which is why I put a lot of emphasis on not waiting for Q4 for bitcoin to bottom.

And so the market will make you miss out the best ways possible, with local pullbacks after fomo bursts, enough to wipe out the high leverage, but also with deeper pullbacks at a nice rule-of-3 rhythm to wipe out lower leverage, then cycling back.

That's just my view, but we're also seeing it around now quite clearly.

Follow at own discretion as always.

Reminder that I still hold and how to navigate in boredom.

Alright, shouldn't be necessary to make this post since I announce every entry and exit.

But to my followers I owe you a reminder per form of standards and good practice.

Also wanted to highlight our main and ongoing thesis of "macro bottom boredom is here" and updating some notes on what that means to trade going forward.

What boredom doesn't mean

What boredom doesn't mean is that we can't trade this market or that it becomes "harder". Not necessarily always. The moves just become smaller, or take longer, and there are more fakeouts.

To some, that can be hard, especially since smaller moves means your profit-to-fee ratio is smaller, and fake-outs are not as fun to trade if you don't know what you're doing.

Finally, the average trader also has almost 0 patience and that certainly gets tested during boredom.

What boredom does mean

So what it means is to counteract all of the above. Which is to firstly continue to expect it, hold for longer and more stubbornly and play the market slower and be more patient as a baseline.

Where one move against the trade in a prime market could mean it's game over and time to get out fast, one move against in a "harder-to-trade" market of boredom, is far more likely the fake-out before a larger move in favour.

All reasons why I'm holding this long, why I still believe this is a market of boredom for some time, small candles will be the norm, but with all parameters above in check, trading it will remain profitable and in fact become easier since moves will be easier to catch and harder to miss.

Those are my thoughts, all NFA, just sharing them, alongside the moves I make trading this market.

Enjoy.

tweets.text:
$btc 

 The trades I am still holding on all timeframes and multi-timeframe plan.

Below an extensive summary of the trades I am still holding and why. This is an execution oriented post, with mild reminders to my plan on how I'm currently positioned for all timeframes.

To the ones who follow me closely, nothing will be new here, but you all like reminders.

It's part of my transparency and good practice, always keeping you up to date of the general positions I am in without oversharing unnecessary details.

I like to frequently remind you since I do trade multiple timeframes. And I always mildly recommend watching multiple timeframes as a form of practice to stay in tune with the market properly, not lose touch, and it allows to keep your plan flexible adhering to the environment we are in, especially with assets of "permanent" accumulation interest.

Macro plan and trades (Monthly/weekly timeframe)

For the monthly timeframe, the plan continues of the ongoing spot accumulation, where we strongly recommended against "DCA-ing", since that never/rarely allows to get enough near the bottom and it doesn't clearly define how much to "DCA", neither does it have proper invalidation.

Our plan is instead to buy 3 batches and adapt dynamically. One early buy, one near the estimated bottom and one confirmation buy.

Since Feb was our early expected bottom time, that was buy 1, in the summer after the 7.12% bounce was buy 2 which beautifully ended up being the bottom so far indeed, and buy 3 waiting for full macro confirmation.

Positional trade: the long (3-Day timeframe or similar)

Then comes one timeframe step down, where we intended to capture the large breakout which took place imo when price aggressively moved above 69k where we took the entry.

I'm still holding that trade even if September turns red, because the trend likely continues imo afterwards, hence why I'm still holding 35% and might increase size again if opportune deep retraces arise.

So despite the confluences of serious resistance 80-83k, it's only local resistance and does not serve a purpose to fully close a trade on the timeframe above.

Swing trade (6-hourly timeframe or similar)

Because that's what the swing trade is for, the short. Detecting resistance, detecting the OHLC, mmd, order flow locally, March 2025 defence, POI etc. On timeframes where a short against the larger trend makes sense.

Acts as a clean hedge against both the positional and macro spot position as well, and is in full alignment with expecting red September where repeated trades or 1 big swing trade of these shorts can be caught, per our stated plan.

Of the current short, still holding 55% waiting for lower.

Scalps (m30 or similar)

Are all trades below that. Trades I share less often, except for the scalp long recently, as a great example of a scalp aiming for those 1000-2000 point moves total. Great trades to take when $btc starts compressing, ranging and getting "boring".

Scalp plan wise, still expecting higher locally as we indeed have been moving before lower.

Final notes

Notice how recently, I was macro spot positioned, positional long, swing short and scalp long, yet all of the trades managed to co-exist and work out and were in alignment with the overall multi-timeframe plan.

That's because the timeframes from macro -> daily/positional -> swing -> scalp are big enough jumps (factor of 12 or similar) to not affect each other.

They also allow to affect each other through bias -> execution when stepping up or down one timeframe.

That brings the beauty of multi timeframe positioning full circle, helps you stay sharp and when the market does something unexpected, still allows you to profit most of the time.

It's imo a myth to align your "personality" with your trading timeframe. Not investing just because you don't have the patience seems like a detrimental issue, or not taking a swing trade while one of the best swing trade opportunities arises, equally.

So with all that said, I disclosed roughly all positions I hold, why and so you know on all timeframes where I expect price to go + actions towards it.

tweets.text:
On finance X, you generally see three things

1️⃣Education
2️⃣Signals
3️⃣"Calls"

1️⃣ is great but if it lacks demonstration it's very random and filler or not proven therefore should be looked very critically upon if true. Or be sent into costly (for both money and your time) rabbit holes of false belief.

2️⃣Signals are great because if done transparently, it showcases the record of a trader in live time. Sadly, transparency often lacks, signals are inconsistent and it becomes hard to track an individual. Aside myself, I am not aware of any other traders sharing high level transparency and weekly frequency in their signals, often abandoning positions or not clearly stating in real time when they enter or exit.

3️⃣Finally, there are calls. Calls are also great in their own way. "I think the market goes in this direction". Great. If people reliably can tell where the market goes, there is value. But perceived value is sadly a lot higher than actual value due to hindsight callbacks and quotes.

Where an idea only becomes clear after the fact.

And frankly, on their own, they are in fact all useless to become a trader.

To become a good trader, all three are needed.

With that framework in mind I continue to share adhering to 1️⃣ 2️⃣ and 3️⃣.

It's the only way for me to help you make gains and learn how to do it yourself.

Welcome and I hope you learn something.
